answer.justification: Hoarseness after thyroidectomy most likely reflects recurrent laryngeal nerve injury causing vocal cord paralysis. The RLN runs in the tracheoesophageal groove and is intimately related to the inferior thyroid artery near the gland; ligating it close to the poles, rather than away from the gland, risks nerve damage. External laryngeal nerve injury weakens cricothyroid (high-pitch voice), internal laryngeal nerve injury causes aspiration, and laryngeal edema produces acute airway symptoms, not delayed hoarseness.
